reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents a PlusToken 2.0 launch and instructs viewers to transfer EOS, enter a tag, and activate AIDoc through that transfer. The displayed warning says an incorrectly handled transfer may not be credited or recoverable, while the speaker frames the reversed deposit and withdrawal wording as an app error reported for correction.

citations.quote: If you want to deposit EOS to activate your AIDoc, must copy the tag and must fill up the tag when you transfer your EOS from Binance or from anywhere into Plus Token okay
if you want to deposit EOS, you click right now, it's the withdrawal button, so you will have the address for EOS and also the tag
If you want to withdraw your Plus tokens in to Bitcoin for example you have to do two actions first, from Plus to Ethereum and ETH then to Bitcoin
so far the company only launches ethereum to all the other currency

opening.argument: The presentation is framed as a cautious product-testing update, not a deceptive solicitation. The speaker says the company is using the next seven days to test the app, identify problems, and fix them, and specifically reports a translation error rather than hiding it. The transfer screen itself visibly warns users about correctly entering the label and the possibility that a transfer may not be recoverable. That combination of disclosed defects, limited rollout, and operational warning is more consistent with an imperfect software demonstration than with concealed scam conduct.

citations.quote: Because next 7 days the company already do the announcement asking offers, testing ahm checking out everything inside the app any problem that we will report to the company and they will change it and they will fix it
On the Chinese and Korean version, they are perfect
And I already reported to the company They will change it very soon

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the transfer warning and reversed labels as evidence of fraud, but those facts support a different reading: the speaker openly identifies the interface problem and says it has been reported for correction. A warning about an incorrectly handled transfer establishes transaction risk, not deceptive intent. The opening also does not show that any transfer occurred, that funds were lost, or that a return was promised.

citations.quote: now they have one big mistake right here on the translation
And I already reported to the company They will change it very soon

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the defect a translation issue does not resolve the central concern: the speaker still directs viewers to use the mislabeled withdrawal control to obtain an address and tag, then transfer EOS to activate AIDoc. The warning underscores that mistakes can make funds unrecoverable; it does not independently verify the service or make the funding instruction safe.

citations.quote: if you want to deposit EOS, you click right now, it's the withdrawal button, so you will have the address for EOS and also the tag
If you want to deposit EOS to activate your AIDoc, must copy the tag and must fill up the tag when you transfer your EOS from Binance or from anywhere into Plus Token okay

opening.argument: This is an operational walkthrough of a cryptocurrency app. The speaker explicitly says he is making a video to go through the app and show something new, then demonstrates where the exchange is located and explains the currently available trading route. The content is instructional: it explains menu navigation, wallet addresses, tags, and exchange pairs. Explaining how software currently works, including its limitations and bugs, does not by itself amount to certifying the platform or soliciting a deceptive investment.

citations.quote: So I just make a video going through the app to show you something new
where is our exchange so when you want to go to exchange, you go to profile and then you will see the coin-currency trading
the next seven days company understand the app still have some little bugs still have little issues

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution describes the tutorial's instructions as proof of a scam, but instructional detail is precisely what an app walkthrough would contain. The speaker does not claim that trading is profitable or guaranteed; he explains that only certain pairs are currently available and that additional exchanges may be added later. Showing a workflow is not the same as promising an outcome from it.

citations.quote: for now company are telling us that they only launching from plus tokens, still only exchanged to but with ETH
one by one because the next seven days company understand the app still have some little bugs still have little issues

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format does not neutralize what is being instructed. The walkthrough connects a cryptocurrency transfer to activating AIDoc and explains how to obtain the address and tag for that transfer. A tutorial can still promote a risky funding mechanism; the absence of an explicit profit guarantee does not answer the concern about directing viewers to deposit assets.

citations.quote: If you want to deposit EOS to activate your AIDoc, must copy the tag and must fill up the tag when you transfer your EOS from Binance or from anywhere into Plus Token okay
you will have the address for EOS and also the tag

opening.argument: The material is best understood as ordinary software and exchange-service information, with visible menus for payments, wallet management, and coin trading. The exchange screen shows selectable pairs such as EOS/ETH and BTC/ETH, while the speaker explains the platform's staged rollout. Crucially, the supplied material does not show a guaranteed return, automated trading result, completed transfer, downline recruitment, or a request for credentials. It describes functionality and limitations, not a demonstrated scam mechanism or assured financial outcome.

citations.quote: so far the company only launches ethereum to all the other currency
later on they will roll out bitcoin against all the other one

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's theory depends on treating any cryptocurrency funding workflow as inherently fraudulent. But the visible exchange interface and the explanation of available pairs are also consistent with an ordinary exchange service. The cited material does not establish a completed payment, promised return, automated bot, or loss. Even the claimed activation step is presented as a technical wallet procedure, not as a guaranteed investment result.

citations.quote: If you want to withdraw your Plus tokens in to Bitcoin for example you have to do two actions first, from Plus to Ethereum and ETH then to Bitcoin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not merely that an exchange screen exists or that a profit guarantee is absent. The speaker specifically instructs viewers to transfer EOS from an outside exchange into PlusToken to activate AIDoc, while the app labels the relevant control as withdrawal. That is a concrete deposit-and-activation workflow, and the lack of a completed transfer in the recording does not make the instruction ordinary or independently safe.
